The words

Welcome, Thou Victor in the strife,
Welcome from out the cave!
To-day we triumph in Thy life
Around Thine empty grave.

Our enemy is put to shame,
His short-lived triumph o’er;
Our God is with us, we exclaim;
We fear our foe no more.

The dwellings of the just resound
With songs of victory;
For in their midst Thou, Lord, art found
And bringest peace with Thee.

O let Thy conquering banner wave
O’er hearts Thou makest free;
And point the path that from the grave
Leads heavenward up to Thee.

We bury all our sin and crime
Deep in our Savior’s tomb
And seek the treasure there that time
And change can ne’er consume.

Fearless we lay us in the tomb
And sleep the night away;
For Thou art there to break the gloom
And call us back to-day.

How to sing it from the solfa

  • Find doh first. Play or hum G and sing d r m f s up from it, so the whole choir has the key in their ears before you start.
  • Pitch the first note. The tune starts on m (B).
  • Count the time. 3/4 means three crotchet beats in each bar. In the grid every cell is half a crotchet: a dash (–) holds the note before it, and _ is a rest.
  • Know the notes. The tune uses d r m f s l t. A comma after a note (s,) is the octave below; an apostrophe (d') is the octave above.

About the hymn

Benjamin Schmolck wrote these words in German. Catherine Winkworth's translation was printed in the Evangelical Lutheran Hymn-Book (St. Louis, 1927), as hymn 228.

The book printed the words without tunes, marked Common Metre (8.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to ST. AGNES; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.

  • Words: Benjamin Schmolck (1672–1737)
  • Translated: Catherine Winkworth (1827–1878)
  • Music (1866): John Bacchus Dykes (1823–1876)

Questions about Welcome, Thou Victor in the Strife

What is the doh of Welcome, Thou Victor in the Strife?

In this version, in G major, doh is G. If your choir sings it in another key, doh moves to the new key note and every solfa syllable stays the same — that is what movable doh means.

What note does Welcome, Thou Victor in the Strife start on?

It starts on m (B in G major). Find doh first, then sing up or down to m.

Is Welcome, Thou Victor in the Strife in the public domain?

Yes. Benjamin Schmolck died in 1737, Catherine Winkworth died in 1878, John Bacchus Dykes died in 1876; the words were in print by 1927 and the music in 1866. Everyone named died before 1955 and both were published before 1929, so the hymn is out of copyright in the UK, the EU, the United States and Nigeria. Modern arrangements and translations can still be under copyright.
